health_system_expense.basis: Duke University Health System, Inc. and Affiliates 'Total expenses' on its separately issued Consolidated Statements of Operations (health-care-organization presentation: FY25 7,105,720 and FY24 6,619,243 thousand from FY25 DUHS report PDF p.6; FY23 4,989,330 from FY24 DUHS report PDF p.6). Cross-check: Duke consolidated total operating expenses minus 'The University (supplementary information, exclusive of DUHS)' Schedule 2 total = FY25 10,953,208-3,858,371 = 7,094,837,000; FY24 10,317,041-3,699,686 = 6,617,355,000; FY23 8,431,382-3,440,506 = 4,990,876,000 (within 0.2% of the DUHS-issued figures). Duke's consolidated statements reclassify some DUHS nonoperating items as operating, so the two bases differ slightly.

university_only_S_W.note: Schedule 2 'The University (exclusive of DUHS)': consolidated S&W minus these = health system and other S&W: FY25 3,073,073,000; FY24 2,915,368,000; FY23 2,023,451,000.

entities_included.other: Duke Health Integrated Practice (DHIP) acquired the Private Diagnostic Clinic (PDC) physician practice July 1, 2023 (most physicians and staff became DUHS employees; FY24 first full year). Duke Health Lake Norman Hospital acquired April 1, 2025. No FFRDC.

calibration_fy23.explanation: S&W: exact match to the consolidated (with DUHS) 'Salaries and wages' 3,676,675 thousand (FY23), benefits excluded. Core opex: the reference 8,431,382,000 equals FY23 TOTAL operating expenses exactly (8,431,382 thousand). Against the SPEC definition (total minus D&A 487,619,000 minus interest 147,882,000 = 7,795,881,000) the reference is 7.5% higher, because the original analysis did not deduct depreciation/amortization or interest.

student_counts_in_official_docs: Yes. Statistical Highlights (FY25 report printed p.9, PDF p.11), 'Total fall enrollment': column 2025 = 17,992 (undergraduate 7,109; graduate and professional 10,883); 2024 = 17,543 (7,034; 10,509); 2023 = 18,009 (7,018; 10,991); 2022 = 17,430; 2021 = 15,793. The table labels its columns by fiscal year (2025 ... 2021) and does not say which fall term is meant (most likely the fall that starts the fiscal year, i.e. Fall 2024 for the 2025 column; confirm before use). Same table gives Faculty and staff: total regular rank faculty 4,230; University staff 27,870; DUHS staff 31,964; total employees 64,064 (2025 column).
caveats: FY23 to FY24 is NOT comparable: Duke's S&W jumps from 3,676,675,000 to 4,762,823,000 (+29.5%) and total operating expenses from 8,431,382,000 to 10,317,041,000 (+22.4%) mainly because DUHS acquired the PDC physician practice on July 1, 2023 (FY24 MD&A: $1.1 billion of DUHS revenue growth from the acquisition, plus $578 million from HASP/340B; HASP also added provider assessments as expense). FY23 was not restated. Use FY24 and FY25 for a like-for-like base; DUHS staff rose from 27,708 (2023) to 30,470 (2024).
Depreciation and amortization is one combined line, so amortization is null; the whole D&A line is subtracted in core opex.

Duke consolidates DUHS under college-and-university presentation, which differs from DUHS's own issued statements: certain DUHS nonoperating components are reclassified as operating in Duke's statements (Duke's FY25 statements include $160 million of net income from DUHS operations versus $179 million operating income in the DUHS-issued statements, per MD&A).
State provider assessments (HASP) expense is inside operating expenses via DUHS (DUHS-issued FY25 333,992,000; FY24 355,865,000; FY23 101,188,000), which inflates FY24-25 opex versus earlier years.
Student aid (FY25 61,432,000) is a separate operating expense line, not S&W or benefits.
Fall enrollment column labeling ambiguity (see student_counts).
